PMID:39583373.topic: Labelling of fluids in the sterile field
PMID:39583373.setting: Orthopaedic department (three orthopaedic theatres, two elective and one trauma) of a district general hospital
PMID:39583373.standard: Royal Pharmaceutical Society and Royal College of Anaesthetists guidelines: all syringes/containers of fluid in the sterile field labelled with fluid name and concentration

cycle1.result: 3/30 procedures (10%) compliant with labelling guidelines; labelling information adequate in only 1 of these 3

PMID:39583373.intervention: Sterile stickers with surgical marker pens for labelling by the scrub nurse, a mandatory 'tactical pause and check' after opening sets, and an awareness campaign (posters, emails, educational sessions)

cycle2.result: 32/34 procedures (94%) compliant (p<0.00001, Fisher's exact test); labelling adequate in 28 of labelled cases

PMID:39583373.other_findings: Baseline reasons for non-compliance were lack of sterile labels, inconvenience at critical moments and human factors. In cycle 2, 3/34 fluids were not labelled immediately after drawing up.

PMID:41311778.topic: Ottawa knee rules compliance for knee radiographs
PMID:41311778.setting: Emergency department, St. Luke's General Hospital, Kilkenny (general hospital)
PMID:41311778.standard: RCR iRefer guidelines: ≥95% of knee radiographs requested in accordance with Ottawa Knee Rules; ≥95% of requests documenting an OKR indication; unnecessary imaging ≤10%

cycle1.result: OKR compliance 50 (72.5%); non-compliant requests 19 (27.5%); documentation of suspected fracture/bone injury 23 (32.9%); negative X-rays 37 (52.9%)

PMID:41311778.intervention: Interactive teaching session for ED clinicians, OKR leaflets distributed and emailed, and posters in ED clinical areas and beside imaging request stations

cycle2.result: OKR compliance 66 (83.5%) (χ²=2.05, p=0.15); non-compliant requests 13 (16.5%); documentation of suspected fracture/bone injury 44 (55.7%) (p=0.01); negative X-rays 30 (38.0%) (p=0.08)

PMID:41311778.other_findings: Compliance remained below the 95% target. Estimated radiographer time saved was about 60-90 minutes per cycle.

PMID:27493729.topic: Hip fracture best practice tariff and mortality
PMID:27493729.setting: St Peter's Hospital, Ashford & St Peter's NHS Trust, orthogeriatric hip fracture service
PMID:27493729.standard: Blue Book standards and hip fracture best practice tariff (including time to theatre within 36 hours), tracked via NHFD

cycle1.result: 39.6% operated within 36 hours (2010); best practice tariff attainment 28% (2010); 30-day mortality 7.8%

PMID:27493729.intervention: Integrated orthogeriatricians; LEAN (EQuIP) pathway redesign with split weekend theatre lists, priority theatre pyramid, new clerking proforma with falls and bone health, A-Z preoperative guide, fast bleep, extra pressure mattresses, seven-day physiotherapy, monthly governance meetings, and measures to prevent post-operative complications and improve Wednesday-admission review

cycle2.result: 84% operated within 36 hours (national 71%); best practice tariff attainment 83% (national 55%); 30-day mortality 5.3% (national 8.2%)

PMID:27493729.other_findings: Peak results in 2012 were 88% within 36 hours and 88% BPT. Pressure ulcers fell from 5.4% to 3.2%, mobilisation within 24 hours rose from 41% to 75%, and Wednesday-admission mortality fell from 9.2% to 1.69%.

PMID:40918923.setting: Orthopaedic Surgery Department, Gezira Traumatology Center, Wad Madani Teaching Hospital
PMID:40918923.standard: Royal College of Surgeons Good Surgical Practice operative note guidance (14 parameters)

cycle1.result: Mean compliance 82.0%; theatre anaesthetist name 1 (4.3%), anticipated blood loss 3 (13%), antibiotic prophylaxis 2 (8.7%), complications 12 (52.2%); procedure 22 (95.7%) and signature 23 (100%)

PMID:40918923.intervention: Staff education, a standardised RCS-aligned operative note template, posters in theatres and staff areas, and a senior feedback mechanism

cycle2.result: Mean compliance 83.4%; anaesthetist name 19 (82.6%), anticipated blood loss 19 (82.6%), antibiotic prophylaxis 16 (69.6%), complications 21 (91.3%)

PMID:40918923.other_findings: Prosthesis identification fell from 20 (87%) to 6 (26.1%) and tissue details from 20 (87%) to 15 (65.2%); incision and closure documentation also declined.

PMID:38143620.topic: Suspected cauda equina syndrome MRI waiting time
PMID:38143620.setting: Wythenshawe Hospital, Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust, a district general hospital with no on-site spinal services; trauma and orthopaedic referrals from the emergency department
PMID:38143620.standard: NICE, BASS and SBNS guidelines and local trust protocol; National Suspected CES Pathway recommends MRI within four hours of request

cycle1.result: Mean MRI waiting time 12.5 hours (8am-4pm 9.5 h; 4pm-12am 18 h; 12am-8am 8.5 h); same-day discharge 27 (29%); inpatient stay 66 (71%)

PMID:38143620.intervention: Introduction of a middle-grade trauma and orthopaedic doctor in the emergency department (urgent treatment centre) to assess suspected CES patients

cycle2.result: Mean MRI waiting time 8 hours (8am-4pm 5.5 h; 4pm-12am 13 h; 12am-8am 6.5 h); all MRI scans and reports within 24 hours; same-day discharge 21 (58%); inpatient stay 15 (42%)

PMID:38143620.other_findings: No patient in cycle 2 had confirmed CES (possible CES in 1, 3%). Admissions fell from an average of 11 to 7 patients per month.

PMID:34660043.topic: Fascia iliaca block for hip fracture
PMID:34660043.setting: District hospital (Salisbury), emergency department and trauma and orthopaedics; NHFD data
PMID:34660043.standard: NICE hip fracture guidance and BOAST fragility fracture analgesia guidance; local decision that all hip fracture patients receive FICB on presentation unless contraindicated

cycle1.result: FICB administered in 45 (24.5%); mean post-FICB pain score 4 (NRS)

PMID:34660043.intervention: Results discussed at departmental and Trust mortality meetings, one-to-one teaching on loss-of-resistance FICB for ED and T&O junior doctors, and enforcing completion of the hip fracture clinical proforma with FICB sign-off or documented contraindication

cycle2.result: FICB administered in 94 (44.3%) (p<0.00001); mean post-FICB pain score 3.6 (p<0.0011)

PMID:34660043.other_findings: The text gives 148 patients in the first audit but the table gives n=184. No FICB complications were recorded; block success rate was 74%.

PMID:33437472.setting: Trauma and Orthopaedic Department, University Hospital of North Tees; elective hip arthroplasty operative notes
PMID:33437472.standard: GIRFT, British Hip Society and BOA July 2019 total hip arthroplasty best practice guidance (24 documentation criteria)

cycle1.result: Handwritten notes scored an average of 12/24 (50%); compliance ranged 0%-100% across criteria, e.g. protection of critical structures 15%, leg length/neurovascular status 20%, intraoperative complications 5%; 80% legible

PMID:33437472.intervention: Pre-populated GIRFT-compliant online hip arthroplasty operative note proforma in the local 'Trackcare' electronic system, typed notes

cycle2.result: Typed notes with the computerised proforma scored an average of 22/24 (92%) (p<0.05); compliance 80%-100% across criteria; 15 of 24 criteria significantly improved; 100% legible

PMID:33437472.other_findings: 25 handwritten notes were collected in cycle 1 and 5 illegible notes excluded. Anaesthetist name and grade stayed at 80%; average documentation time fell from 25 to 7 minutes.

PMID:19284645.setting: Eight NHS community podiatry departments in the Trent and South Yorkshire region

cycle1.result: Podiatry Health Questionnaire score improved from mean 11.8 to 11.2 and pain VAS from 4.8 to 4.1 two weeks after treatment (p<0.0001); 75% of patients stayed the same or improved

PMID:19284645.other_findings: Before-and-after outcome audit with no standard; 25% of patients reported worse scores after treatment and the improvements were small.

PMID:25908945.topic: Complications of minimally invasive lesser toe surgery
PMID:25908945.setting: Single surgeon's practice, procedures in office procedure rooms and hospitals/surgi-centres on a day-case basis
PMID:25908945.standard: Australasian College of Podiatric Surgeons surgical audit clinical indicators (developed from the ACHS clinical indicator program); compared with published complication rates for open digital surgery

cycle1.result: 299 digits operated on; 1 superficial infection (0.56%), 2 under-corrections needing revision (0.67%); no other ACPS indicator events, no neurovascular or medical complications

PMID:25908945.other_findings: Two patients (0.7%) had pain from delayed union at 4 months that resolved by 6 months. 45% of procedures were done in an office setting without fluoroscopy.

PMID:31428650.setting: Tertiary referral hospital, Clinical Center Nis

cycle1.result: Plate (n=36) versus IM nail (n=20): union 100% versus 90%; mean Constant-Murley score 82.40 versus 77.58 (p=0.246); complications 13.8% versus 10%

PMID:31428650.other_findings: Retrospective comparative outcome study; IM nailing had significantly lower blood loss, shorter surgery and shorter hospital stay (all p<0.001).

PMID:40761982.setting: Emergency department and trauma unit, The Grange University Hospital, Aneurin Bevan University Health Board
PMID:40761982.standard: Health board clinical pathway for traumatic anterior shoulder instability, aligned with BOA and BESS guidance (pre- and post-reduction radiographs, neurovascular assessment, specialist follow-up)

cycle1.result: Pre- and post-reduction radiographs in 97/100 (97%), post-reduction only in 3 (3%); MUA successful in 98 (98%); mean time to reduction 152 minutes; nerve injury in 28 (28%)

PMID:40761982.other_findings: Not all patients under 40 received an MR arthrogram as recommended. Posterior dislocations made up 16% of cases and 10 patients were lost to follow-up.

PMID:41393555.topic: Distal radius fracture time to surgery
PMID:41393555.setting: Department of Trauma and Orthopaedic Surgery, University Hospital Waterford (regional trauma centre), day-case trauma lists
PMID:41393555.standard: BOAST distal radius fracture guidance: intra-articular fractures operated within 72 hours and extra-articular within seven days; local target ≥80%

cycle1.result: Intra-articular within 3 days of injury 16/27 (59%); extra-articular within 7 days of injury 24/26 (92%); intra-articular within 3 days of referral 20/27 (74%)

PMID:41393555.intervention: Staff education on BOAST guidance for doctors and trauma coordinators at the morbidity and mortality meeting (PDSA 1), then repeat education and changing the trauma list spreadsheet dropdown to separate intra-articular and extra-articular distal radius fractures (PDSA 2)

cycle2.result: Intra-articular within 3 days of injury 24/32 (75%) (p=0.2665; p trend=0.1924); extra-articular within 7 days of injury 13/19 (68%) (p=0.0119; p trend=0.0243); intra-articular within 3 days of referral 28/32 (88%)

PMID:41393555.other_findings: Second cycle (April to June 2024, n=57): intra-articular within 3 days of injury 14/25 (56%) and extra-articular within 7 days 31/32 (97%). Intra-articular timeliness stayed below the 80% target and extra-articular timeliness fell in the final cycle.

PMID:37362517.setting: Orthopaedics department, MVJ Medical College and Research Hospital, tertiary care hospital, Bangalore
PMID:37362517.standard: Standard discharge summary checklist from a systematic review (predetermined set of criteria)

cycle1.dates: Audited between May 22 and October 22 (handwritten summaries, before electronic summaries introduced on 8 January 2022)
cycle1.result: Handwritten summaries: complications in hospital 50%, contact information 34%, condition at discharge 66%, understandability 58%, allergies 66%, problem list/issues pending 35%, discharge medications 88%, follow-up plan 80%; patient signature 0%

PMID:37362517.intervention: Introduction of electronic discharge summaries using a standardised form completed by orthopaedic residents (from 8 January 2022)

cycle2.result: Electronic summaries: complications in hospital 100%, contact information 95%, condition at discharge 96%, understandability 100%, allergies 100%, problem list/issues pending 92%, discharge medications 100%, follow-up plan 100%; patient signature 100%

PMID:37362517.other_findings: Social issues, cultural concepts, support to relatives, palliative care information, discharge destination, clinical trial involvement and sick note were documented in 0% of both handwritten and electronic summaries. No statistical testing was done.

PMID:7574306.setting: Royal National Orthopaedic Hospital, Stanmore; senior registrar appointments
PMID:7574306.other_findings: Abstract only: analysis of the CVs of 50 trainees appointed as senior registrars to identify the normal pattern of educational achievement.
